title: Welcome to the club, guys.
author: Fair_Ad_9505
selftext:
Over the last couple of day's i've seen plenty of posts of people complaining about how inflated the industry is now, all the slop thats going to get posted. people losing motivation etc.

I want to let you in on a secret. AI becoming as strong as it is for gaming is going to make things great, and worse all at the same time.

Just for backround i've been a musician for about 10 years. i've made my little bits of cash here and there and overall had a good enough time with it. now in rap music specifically, people started to have the same sentiments that the gaming industry has now around 2016 when the XXL cover dropped. lts of older guys and purists getting upset because all the rappers on there were 'mumble rappers'. nothing they said changed anything, trends continued and music grew to what it's grown too. but how were they able to get this far? it was soundcloud.

soundcloud is what happens when you bring gatekept information down to the common man. it was a free distrobutor that exposed artists to millions of people. additionally at the same time studio equipment got cheaper and cheaper to the point were most AAA albums made today are recorded in the bedroom of someones house.

With distrobution / equipment becoming more availble people were able to really just sit down and create without needing to know a bunch of people or even have that much knowledge about music in the first place. this gave birth to what people think 'mumble rap' is. through that, the creative glass was shattered and people came by and grabbed the peices, returned to were they came from and made something new. it was a literal explosion of color and sounds and ideas that we had never seen before in music because traditionally, you woulda had to have known someone with connections or a shit load of money to even have the chance to record something. but now? well anyone can do it. in turn with soundcloud, the market got flooded, anyone who jumped on the train early, or had already been on the train were the first to get their share of the pot, but slowly over time the market got more and more saturated, and now its sooooo hard to make a name. because a million people are making noise so trying to get one person to hear you is a big fucking ask lol.

So, whats this got to do with gaming? well the distrobution has been here, steam. so getting your games published definity isn't a gatekept endevour. the equipment? well i mean, unity and ue5 are both free, same with blender, you just need a decent enough pc to run these things. so what the problem?

knowledge.

now knowledge is free, plenty of tutorials and shit you can watch. hours and hours of content you can consume to get better at the craft. but thats just for the engine, you need to know how to 3d design, code, system design. making a video game alone (even now with AI) is a big fucking task.

But AI is soundcloud, its brining all that knowledge down to the people who never took the time to learn and saying "hey, you can do this too. ever have an idea for a game?"

So in the next few years, we will see some dogshit for sure lol. it would be stupid to think otherwise. but theres been dogshit here before so thats nothing new, whats worse is that the market is going to flood like crazy, and the better AI gets at making games the harder its going to be to make it out. so get started now is my best advice.

However, these next few years we will also see the same explosion of color and noise that we saw in 2016 and even 2020 with music. the glass is breaking, and people are rushing over to grab themselves a piece and go home to make something new with it.

And to be fair, making a video game is still hard even with AI, especially if you're going for a niche style in the art department, small tangent but ive tried those 3d editors and i hate them. i just found an artist instead so now i can put "ethically sourced assets" on the box lol.

Long live the arts. AI wont replace us, it will only make more of us.
